# survalis

Unified survival machine learning and interpretability in R.

`survalis` provides a unified framework for survival machine learning in
R. Seven verbs cover the whole workflow for 22 built-in learners and for
any learner you write yourself: fitting, prediction, resampled and
external evaluation, tuning, paired comparison, model-agnostic
interpretation, and causal contrasts.

`survalis` is available on CRAN:
<https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=survalis>.

## The seven-verb interface

``` r

library(survalis)
f <- Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype

m   <- fit(f, veteran, model = "ranger", spec = list(num.trees = 500))
predict(m, veteran[1:5, ], times = c(90, 180, 365))          # survival matrix
evaluate(m, times = c(90, 180, 365), resampling = cv(5))     # resampled metrics

cmp <- compare(f, veteran, models = c("coxph", "ranger", "densemlp"),
               times = c(90, 180, 365))
plot(cmp)

plot(interpret(m, "shap", newdata = veteran[1, ], times = 180))
estimate(f, veteran, model = "ranger", treatment = "trt", tau = 365)
```

[`fit()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/fit.md),
[`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html),
[`evaluate()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/evaluate.md),
[`tune()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/tune.md),
[`compare()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/compare.md),
[`interpret()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/interpret.md)
and
[`estimate()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/estimate.md)
are the whole interface. Resampling is described by
[`cv()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/resampling.md),
[`holdout()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/resampling.md),
[`group_cv()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/resampling.md)
and
[`bootstrap()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/resampling.md),
and
[`list_survlearners()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/list_survlearners.md),
[`list_metrics()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/list_metrics.md)
and
[`list_interpretability_methods()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/list_interpretability_methods.md)
give the valid ids. Upgrading from 1.x? See
[`vignette("from-1.0", package = "survalis")`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/articles/from-1.0.md).

## Installation

``` r

# Install the released version from CRAN
install.packages("survalis")

# Or install the development version from GitHub
remotes::install_github("ielbadisy/survalis")
```

## Core philosophy

- Seven verbs cover the whole workflow:
  [`fit()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/fit.md),
  [`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html),
  [`evaluate()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/evaluate.md),
  [`tune()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/tune.md),
  [`compare()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/compare.md),
  [`interpret()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/interpret.md),
  [`estimate()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/estimate.md)
- One function per job: learners are chosen by `model`, metrics by
  `metrics`, explanations by `method`, outputs by `type`
- Every verb returns an S3 object with
  [`print()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/print.html),
  [`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html),
  [`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) and
  [`as.data.frame()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/as.data.frame.html) methods
- Matrix predictions are survival matrices: one row per subject, columns
  `t=100`, `t=200`, …, with the grid recorded in `attr(x, "times")`
- A custom learner is two functions, `list(fit = , predict = )`, and
  works with every verb

## Exploring the package

``` r

library(survalis)
list_survlearners()               # ids for `model`
#>            learner tunable
#> 1            coxph   FALSE
#> 2            aalen   FALSE
#> 3           glmnet    TRUE
#> 4        selectcox    TRUE
#> 5           aftgee   FALSE
#> 6      flexsurvreg    TRUE
#> 7          bnnsurv    TRUE
#> 8            rpart    TRUE
#> 9             bart    TRUE
#> 10         xgboost    TRUE
#> 11        coxboost    TRUE
#> 12         fastgbm   FALSE
#> 13          ranger    TRUE
#> 14             rsf    TRUE
#> 15         cforest    TRUE
#> 16      blackboost    TRUE
#> 17         survsvm    TRUE
#> 18        densemlp   FALSE
#> 19            orsf    TRUE
#> 20          rpsurv   FALSE
#> 21          nbsurv   FALSE
#> 22 survmetalearner   FALSE
list_metrics()                    # ids for `metrics`
#>   metric direction
#> 1 cindex  maximize
#> 2    auc  maximize
#> 3  brier  minimize
#> 4    ibs  minimize
#> 5    iae  minimize
#> 6    ise  minimize
#> 7    ece  minimize
#>                                                                    summary
#> 1                Harrell-style concordance index for survival predictions.
#> 2     Cumulative/dynamic time-dependent AUC at a selected evaluation time.
#> 3 Brier Score at specified evaluation time(s) (IPCW-weighted when needed).
#> 4     Integrated Brier Score over an evaluation time grid (IPCW-weighted).
#> 5                Integrated absolute error against the Kaplan-Meier curve.
#> 6                 Integrated squared error against the Kaplan-Meier curve.
#> 7                  Expected calibration error at a single evaluation time.
#>                        range
#> 1  [0, 1] (higher is better)
#> 2  [0, 1] (higher is better)
#> 3   [0, 1] (lower is better)
#> 4   [0, 1] (lower is better)
#> 5 [0, Inf) (lower is better)
#> 6 [0, Inf) (lower is better)
#> 7   [0, 1] (lower is better)
list_interpretability_methods()   # ids for `method` in interpret()
#>            method
#> 1             pdp
#> 2             ice
#> 3             ale
#> 4            shap
#> 5     shap_matrix
#> 6          varimp
#> 7         permute
#> 8     interaction
#> 9  counterfactual
#> 10      surrogate
#> 11 tree_surrogate
#> 12    calibration
#> 13            roc
#> 14            dca
#> 15    survcluster
#>                                                                    summary
#> 1      Partial dependence of predicted survival on one feature, over time.
#> 2               Individual conditional expectation curves for one feature.
#> 3                               Accumulated local effects for one feature.
#> 4                   Shapley values for one instance, aggregated over time.
#> 5                       Shapley values for many instances (beeswarm plot).
#> 6                   Permutation variable importance on the survival scale.
#> 7                                                         Alias of varimp.
#> 8                   Friedman H-statistic interaction strength per feature.
#> 9  Smallest feature changes that move predicted survival at a target time.
#> 10               Local linear surrogate for one instance at a target time.
#> 11                      Global decision-tree surrogate of the predictions.
#> 12                                          Calibration curve at one time.
#> 13                                   Time-dependent ROC curve at one time.
#> 14          Decision curve (net benefit over risk thresholds) at one time.
#> 15            Clusters of subjects with similar predicted survival curves.
```

## Basic Workflow

**1. Fit a model**

``` r

mod_cox <- fit(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype, veteran, model = "coxph")
mod_cox
#> <survalis_fit> model = coxph  (engine: survival)
#>   formula: Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype
#>   data:    137 obs, 128 events (93%)
```

**2. Predict survival probabilities**

``` r

pred <- predict(mod_cox, newdata = veteran[1:5, ], times = c(100, 200))
pred
#> <survmat> survival  |  5 obs x 2 times  [100, 200]
#>          t=100     t=200
#> [1,] 0.6142681 0.3541697
#> [2,] 0.6944383 0.4599242
#> [3,] 0.5556797 0.2860796
#> [4,] 0.6033305 0.3408724
#> [5,] 0.6959633 0.4620783
```

[`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html) also returns other
quantities via `type`: `"risk"` (1 - S(t)), `"chf"`, `"hazard"`,
`"rmst"`, `"quantile"`, `"median"`.

**3. Evaluate model performance**

``` r

ev <- evaluate(mod_cox, times = c(80, 160), resampling = cv(5, seed = 123))
ev
#> <survalis_eval> model = coxph
#> <survalis_resampling> 5-fold CV, strata = status, seed = 123
#>   grid: 2 times in [80, 160]
#>   cindex  0.7180  (sd 0.0530, 95% [0.6720, 0.7640], n = 5)
#>   ibs     0.1820  (sd 0.0420, 95% [0.1460, 0.2190], n = 5)
```

``` r

summary(ev)
#>   metric  mean    sd n    se lower upper
#> 1 cindex 0.718 0.053 5 0.023 0.672 0.764
#> 2    ibs 0.182 0.042 5 0.019 0.146 0.219
```

To score a model on data it was not trained on, pass `newdata`; to score
predictions made elsewhere, pass the survival matrix and the outcome.

``` r

train <- veteran[1:100, ]
test  <- veteran[-(1:100), ]
m_tr  <- fit(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype, train, model = "coxph")
evaluate(m_tr, newdata = test, times = c(80, 160))
#> <survalis_eval> model = coxph
#>   scored once on 37 subjects (no resampling)
#>   grid: 2 times in [80, 160]
#>   cindex  0.7470
#>   ibs     0.1720

S <- predict(m_tr, test, times = c(80, 160))
evaluate(S, y = Surv(test$time, test$status))
#> <survalis_eval> model = supplied predictions
#>   scored once on 37 subjects (no resampling)
#>   grid: 2 times in [80, 160]
#>   cindex  0.7470
#>   ibs     0.1720
```

**4. Compare multiple learners**

[`compare()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/compare.md)
evaluates every learner on the *same* resampling folds, so results are
paired; `tune = TRUE` tunes each tunable learner first.

``` r

cmp <- compare(
  Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype,
  data = veteran,
  models = c("coxph", "rpart", "ranger"),
  times = c(80, 160),
  resampling = cv(3, seed = 1)
  )

cmp
#> <survalis_compare> 3 models
#> <survalis_resampling> 3-fold CV, strata = status, seed = 1
#> 
#>   cindex (higher is better):
#>    * coxph            0.7307  (se 0.0188)
#>      rpart            0.7073  (se 0.0171)
#>      ranger           0.6890  (se 0.0239)
#> 
#>   ibs (lower is better):
#>    * coxph            0.1790  (se 0.0055)
#>      ranger           0.1990  (se 0.0042)
#>      rpart            0.2160  (se 0.0062)
plot(cmp)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-10-1.png)

**5. Bring your own learner**

A custom learner is a list with a `fit` function and a `predict`
function that returns one row per subject and one column per time. It
then works with every verb.

``` r

expo <- list(
  name = "exponential",
  fit = function(formula, data, ...) survival::survreg(formula, data, dist = "exponential"),
  predict = function(object, newdata, times) {
    rate <- 1 / predict(object, newdata, type = "response")
    exp(-outer(rate, times))
  }
)

compare(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype, veteran,
        models = list("coxph", expo), times = c(80, 160),
        resampling = cv(3, seed = 1))
#> <survalis_compare> 2 models
#> <survalis_resampling> 3-fold CV, strata = status, seed = 1
#> 
#>   cindex (higher is better):
#>    * exponential      0.7330  (se 0.0200)
#>      coxph            0.7307  (se 0.0188)
#> 
#>   ibs (lower is better):
#>    * exponential      0.1787  (se 0.0033)
#>      coxph            0.1790  (se 0.0055)
```

**6. Visualize interpretation**

[`interpret()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/interpret.md)
is the single entry point to every explanation method, and
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) draws its
result.

``` r

shap_meanabs <- interpret(
  mod_cox, "shap",
  newdata     = veteran[100, ],
  times       = 80,
  sample.size = 50,
  aggregate   = TRUE,
  shap_method = "meanabs"
  )

as.data.frame(shap_meanabs)
#>           feature         phi
#> trt           trt 0.000000000
#> celltype celltype 0.005120004
#> karno       karno 0.036640340
#> diagtime diagtime 0.000000000
#> age           age 0.003908879
#> prior       prior 0.000000000
```

``` r

plot(shap_meanabs)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-13-1.png)

### More interpretability methods

`survalis` also provides PDP, ALE, surrogate explanations, tree
surrogates, permutation importance, interaction analysis, and
counterfactuals, all through `interpret(fit, method = ..., ...)`.

**Partial dependence and ICE**

``` r

pdp_age <- interpret(mod_cox, "pdp", feature = "age", times = c(100, 200, 300))

plot(pdp_age, which = "per_time")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-14-1.png)

``` r

plot(pdp_age, which = "integrated", smooth = TRUE)
#> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-14-2.png)

**Accumulated local effects**

``` r

ale_karno <- interpret(mod_cox, "ale", feature = "karno", times = c(100, 200, 300))

plot(ale_karno, which = "per_time")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-15-1.png)

``` r

plot(ale_karno, which = "integrated", smooth = TRUE)
#> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-15-2.png)

**Local surrogate explanation**

``` r

local_surrogate <- interpret(
  mod_cox, "surrogate",
  newdata     = veteran[1, , drop = FALSE],
  times       = c(100, 200, 300),
  target_time = 200,
  k           = 5
  )

as.data.frame(local_surrogate)
#>    feature feature_value      effect target_time
#> 1    karno            60 0.491034890         200
#> 2 celltype      squamous 0.189632633         200
#> 3      age            69 0.120729843         200
#> 4 diagtime             7 0.001800378         200
#> 5    prior             0 0.000000000         200
plot(local_surrogate, top_n = 10)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-16-1.png)

**Tree surrogate**

``` r

tree_surrogate <- interpret(mod_cox, "tree_surrogate", times = c(100, 200, 300))

plot(tree_surrogate, type = "importance", top_n = 5)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-17-1.png)

``` r

# plot(tree_surrogate, type = "tree")
```

**Permutation variable importance**

``` r

varimp_res <- interpret(
  mod_cox, "varimp",
  times          = c(100, 200, 300),
  metric         = "ibs",
  n_repetitions  = 5,
  seed           = 123
  )

as.data.frame(varimp_res)
#> # basetable: 6 x 5
#>    feature importance importance_05 importance_95 scaled_importance
#> 1    karno     0.0672        0.0494        0.0826         100.00000
#> 2 celltype     0.0468        0.0394        0.0574          69.64286
#> 3      age    -0.0022       -0.0030       -0.0012           3.27381
#> 4      trt     0.0000        0.0000        0.0000           0.00000
#> 5 diagtime     0.0000        0.0000        0.0000           0.00000
#> 6    prior     0.0000        0.0000        0.0000           0.00000
plot(varimp_res)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-18-1.png)

**Feature interactions**

``` r

interaction_1way <- interpret(mod_cox, "interaction", times = c(100, 200, 300),
                              target_time = 200, type = "1way")
interaction_heatmap <- interpret(mod_cox, "interaction", times = c(100, 200, 300),
                                 target_time = 200, type = "heatmap")
interaction_time <- interpret(mod_cox, "interaction", times = c(100, 200, 300),
                              type = "time")

plot(interaction_1way, type = "1way")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-19-1.png)

``` r

plot(interaction_heatmap, type = "heatmap")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-19-2.png)

``` r

plot(interaction_time, type = "time")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-19-3.png)

**Counterfactual explanations**

``` r

counterfactuals <- interpret(
  mod_cox, "counterfactual",
  newdata            = veteran[1, , drop = FALSE],
  times              = c(100, 200, 300),
  target_time        = 200,
  features_to_change = c("age", "karno", "diagtime"),
  cost_penalty       = 0.01
  )

as.data.frame(counterfactuals)
#>    feature original_value suggested_value survival_gain change_cost
#> 1    karno             60         81.0202        0.2347     21.0202
#> 2 diagtime              7          7.0808        0.0000      0.0808
#> 3      age             69         69.1313        0.0003      0.1313
#>   penalized_gain
#> 1         0.0245
#> 2        -0.0008
#> 3        -0.0010
```

**7. Calibration, ROC and decision curves**

``` r

interpret(mod_cox, "calibration", eval_time = 80, n_bins = 10, n_boot = 30) |> plot()
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-21-1.png)

``` r

interpret(m_tr, "roc", newdata = test, eval_time = 80) |> plot()
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-21-2.png)

``` r
interpret(m_tr, "dca", newdata = test, eval_time = 80) |> plot()
```

# Package index

## Verbs

Fit a learner, predict, evaluate, compare, tune, interpret and estimate
contrasts from one formula and one dataset. Every learner, built in or
your own, goes in `model`.

- [`fit()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/fit.md) : Fit a
  survival learner
- [`predict(`*`<survalis_fit>`*`)`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/predict.survalis_fit.md)
  : Predict from a fitted survival learner
- [`evaluate()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/evaluate.md)
  : Performance of a survival learner
- [`compare()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/compare.md)
  : Compare several survival learners on shared resampling folds
- [`tune()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/tune.md) : Tune
  a survival learner over a hyperparameter grid
- [`interpret()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/interpret.md)
  : Interpret a fitted survival learner
- [`estimate()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/estimate.md)
  : Standardised causal-style contrast for a binary treatment
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<survalis_eval>`*`)`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/survalis-tidiers.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<survalis_tune>`*`)`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/survalis-tidiers.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<survalis_compare>`*`)`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/survalis-tidiers.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<survalis_estimate>`*`)`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/survalis-tidiers.md)
  : Tidy data frames from verb result objects
- [`survalis`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/survalis-package.md)
  [`survalis-package`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/survalis-package.md)
  : survalis: Interpretable Survival Machine Learning

## Resampling

Split schemes used by
[`evaluate()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/evaluate.md),
[`compare()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/compare.md),
[`tune()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/tune.md) and
[`estimate()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/estimate.md).

- [`cv()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/resampling.md)
  [`holdout()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/resampling.md)
  [`group_cv()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/resampling.md)
  [`bootstrap()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/resampling.md)
  : Resampling specifications for evaluate(), tune() and compare()

## Lookups

Valid ids for `model`, `metrics` and `method`.

- [`list_survlearners()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/list_survlearners.md)
  : List the survival learners
- [`list_metrics()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/list_metrics.md)
  : List the evaluation metrics
- [`list_interpretability_methods()`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/list_interpretability_methods.md)
  : List the interpretability methods

## Data and re-exports

- [`veteran`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/veteran.md) :
  Veteran's Administration Lung Cancer Trial Data
- [`reexports`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/reexports.md)
  [`Surv`](https://elbadisyimad.com/survalis/reference/reexports.md) :
  Re-export Surv from survival
